# The History of the Roman Empire

The Roman Empire stands as one of the most influential civilizations in human history, shaping law, government, architecture, and culture across Europe and beyond. Its remarkable journey from a small city-state on the Italian Peninsula to a vast Mediterranean superpower spans over a millennium and continues to influence modern society in countless ways.

## The Founding and Kingdom Period

According to tradition, Rome was founded in 753 BCE by Romulus and Remus, twin brothers raised by a she-wolf. The city began as a monarchy ruled by seven legendary kings, including the brutal Tarquin the Proud, whose expulsion in 509 BCE marked the end of the Roman Kingdom and the beginning of the Roman Republic.

## The Roman Republic

The Republic introduced a complex governmental system featuring elected magistrates, a powerful Senate, and popular assemblies. Roman expansion began systematically during this period, with conquests of the Italian Peninsula followed by the Punic Wars against Carthage. General Scipio Africanus defeated the legendary Carthaginian general Hannibal at Zama in 202 BCE, establishing Roman dominance in the western Mediterranean
